orgs: AmpC producers (Enterobacter, C. freundii, K. aerogenes, Serratia)

classes.Penicillins: Bind penicillin-binding proteins and block cell-wall synthesis (bactericidal). Time-dependent killing: aim for the free drug to stay above the MIC for ≥ 50% of the dosing interval (≥ 100% in critical illness); frequent dosing or prolonged infusions help.
classes.Cephalosporins: β-lactams that block cell-wall synthesis. Time-dependent: target fT>MIC ≥ 60–70% of the interval (100% in critical illness). No activity against enterococci or Listeria.
classes.Carbapenems and monobactams: β-lactams that block cell-wall synthesis, stable to most ESBL and AmpC enzymes (carbapenems). Time-dependent: carbapenems need fT>MIC ≥ 40%; extended infusions help in critical illness.
classes.Aminoglycosides: Bind the 30S ribosome (bactericidal) with a post-antibiotic effect. Concentration-dependent: Cmax/MIC ≥ 8–10 and AUC/MIC 80–100, hence once-daily dosing. Inactive in anaerobic and acidic environments (abscess).
classes.Glycopeptides and lipopeptides: Glycopeptides bind D-Ala-D-Ala and block cell-wall synthesis; daptomycin depolarises the cell membrane. Gram-positive only.
classes.Oxazolidinones: Bind the 50S ribosome (mostly bacteriostatic). Gram-positive only, including MRSA and VRE.
classes.Macrolides and lincosamides: Bind the 50S ribosome (bacteriostatic). Macrolides cover atypicals; clindamycin covers anaerobes and suppresses toxin production.
classes.Tetracyclines: Bind the 30S ribosome (bacteriostatic). Broad spectrum including atypicals and many intracellular organisms.
classes.Quinolones: Inhibit DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV (bactericidal). Concentration-dependent: fAUC/MIC ≥ 100–125 for Gram-negatives, ≥ 30–50 for pneumococcus. Excellent oral bioavailability.
classes.Folate antagonists: Block folate synthesis (trimethoprim: dihydrofolate reductase; sulfamethoxazole: dihydropteroate synthase).
classes.Urinary agents: Concentrated in urine with little or no useful level in blood or tissue: lower urinary tract infection only.
classes.Nitroimidazoles: Reduced inside anaerobes to radicals that damage DNA (bactericidal). Concentration-dependent.
classes.Polymyxins: Cationic peptides that disrupt the outer membrane of Gram-negatives (bactericidal). Narrow therapeutic window.
